justification.synthesis_rationale: Beginning with a cautious anchor around 0.32 (low base-rate) and applying both upward and downward updates from structural bias, potential unity, and poll dynamics, the net effect yields a calibrated posterior near 0.47. Correlations among factors are acknowledged, and calibration accounts for residual uncertainty in turnout and coalition dynamics.

question: Will any political party or coalition acquire a supermajority in the 2026 Hungarian parliamentary elections?
summary: The objections highlight that Hungary's disproportional electoral system can translate modest vote shares into outsized seat shares, increasing the odds of a 2/3 majority under favorable conditions.
A united opposition behind a single front could raise the chances if they secure roughly 44–54% of the vote and capitalize on the seat bonus.

Current polling shows divergent signals with no clear consensus on a 2/3 outcome, suggesting the probability remains uncertain but potentially higher than the ensemble suggests due to structural bias.
Turnout dynamics and mobilization could tilt seats toward either bloc; outcomes are contingent on which side mobilizes more effectively.
Historical precedent shows 2/3 majorities under favorable conditions, though those conditions are not currently strongly evidenced by the latest data.

justification.critique_assessment: The objections validly identify blind spots in the ensemble related to electoral design and potential coalitions, though current polling remains mixed and uncertain.
justification.adjustment: Increased from 0.43 to 0.55 to reflect plausible tail scenarios involving disproportionality and possible opposition consolidation; no implausible threshold assumptions were invoked.

forecasts.reference-class: Two-thirds majority in the 199-seat Hungarian Parliament (133+ seats) under the post-2011 electoral framework (mixed-member with winner-compensation).

sources.claim: Seat projections in early 2026 show around 111 seats for the leading bloc, well short of the 133-seat two-thirds threshold.
Real-PR seat calculator projected Fidesz-KDNP around 64% of parliamentary seats in a hypothetical election today, near but typically below a two-thirds majority.
Prediction markets show mixed expectations; Polymarket odds favored the opposition and Péter Magyar in some readings, with opposing signals across markets.
The electoral system is highly disproportional and strongly favors Fidesz; 44-54% of votes historically translated into about 67-68% of seats.
Pattern shows Fidesz converts roughly 45-54% of votes into 67-68% of seats due to winner-compensation in the Hungarian system.
Medián poll (Nov 25, 2025) shows TISZA leading 50% to 40% for Fidesz, implying incumbents would not reach a two-thirds majority under that snapshot.
Nézőpont poll (Jan 2025) found 61% of active voters prefer waiting until 2026; 33% support an early election.
In 2010, Fidesz won a two-thirds parliamentary majority (263 of 386 seats).
The 2014 election preserved Fidesz-KDNP's two-thirds majority (133 of 199 seats).
The 2018 election again produced a two-thirds majority for Fidesz-KDNP (133 of 199 seats).
The 2022 election gave Fidesz-KDNP a two-thirds majority (134 seats).
Euronews reports divergent polls: some show Tisza ahead, others show Fidesz leading.
Nézőpont poll (Feb 11, 2026): Fidesz 46.0%, TISZA 40.0%.
Závecz Research (Jan 2026) shows Tisza lead in several measures; Medián/IDEA also show Tisza leads in various measures.
HVG reports Závecz Research January 2026 finding Tisza ahead in several metrics.
Hungary Today reports Real-PR seat calculator (via 21 Research Center) projecting Fidesz–KDNP with around 64% of seats, a government majority near two-thirds.
Euronews summarizes polls showing divergent outcomes with some surveys showing Tisza ahead and others showing Fidesz ahead; no consensus on securing a 2/3 majority.
Financial Times reports opposition groups uniting behind Tisza; polls indicate Tisza leads in some surveys, suggesting a potential shift but not an assured path to a 2/3 majority.
Wikipedia's summary of 2026 polling shows multiple firms with varying leads (Medián, Nézőpont, 21 RC) and no consistent path to a 2/3 majority; coalition outcomes vary.
Polymarket shows betting-market odds for the election winner with an implied probability around 62% for Tisza, reflecting uncertainty around a 2/3 majority.

causal-factors.name: Electoral-system disproportionality bias toward the largest party (winner-compensation)
causal-factors.rationale: The Hungarian system historically translates roughly 44–54% of votes into about 67–68% of seats, increasing the odds that a leading bloc reaches 133+ seats even without a landslide.

causal-factors.name: Opposition unity behind a single front (e.g., TISZA)
causal-factors.rationale: A united opposition can concentrate votes and potentially reach the 133-seat threshold, shifting the odds away from a single-party majority.

causal-factors.name: Poll volatility and lack of consensus among major pollsters (Feb 2026)
causal-factors.rationale: Divergent polls (e.g., leads for TISZA vs. Fidesz across firms) reduce confidence in a path to a 2/3 majority.

causal-factors.name: Turnout dynamics and mobilization effects
causal-factors.rationale: Higher turnout and mobilization of supporters for the leading bloc can translate into more seats under disproportional rules.

causal-factors.name: Historical precedent of 2/3 majorities under favorable conditions
causal-factors.rationale: Past elections (2010, 2014, 2018, 2022) show the dominant party can reach a 2/3 majority when conditions favor them.

causal-factors.name: Opposition consolidation into a unified bloc (TISZA)
causal-factors.rationale: Consolidation into a unified opposition bloc (TISZA) could raise the odds of a 2/3 majority if it wins around 44–54% of the vote, which under Hungary's winner-compensation system translates to about 67–68% of seats ([osw.waw.pl](https://www.osw.waw.pl/en/publikacje/osw-commentary/2025-06-05/year-peter-magyar-great-expectations-great-challenges?utm_source=openai))

causal-factors.name: Electoral-system disproportionality and winner-compensation amplifying lead blocs
causal-factors.rationale: The current winner-compensation mechanism amplifies seat shares for the leading bloc, with 44–54% of votes historically translating to about 67–68% of seats, increasing the probability that a united bloc could reach 2/3 ([osw.waw.pl](https://www.osw.waw.pl/en/publikacje/osw-commentary/2025-06-05/year-peter-magyar-great-expectations-great-challenges?utm_source=openai))

causal-factors.name: Persistent polling divergence across firms
causal-factors.rationale: Diverging polls in early 2026 show Fidesz-led results in some surveys and TISZA-led results in others, reducing confidence in a deterministic path to a 2/3 majority ([euronews.com](https://www.euronews.com/2026/02/19/hungarian-polls-split-on-april-election-outcome-as-fidesz-and-tisza-trade-leads?utm_source=openai))

causal-factors.name: Late-2025 polls showing TISZA leads in several measures
causal-factors.rationale: Late-2025 polls show TISZA leading in several measures (e.g., Medián 50–40; Nézőpont 47–40), signaling a potential path to a 2/3 majority if mobilization and turnout favor the opposition ([politpro.eu](https://politpro.eu/en/hungary/opinion-polls/median-2025-11-25/hungary?utm_source=openai))

causal-factors.name: Opposition fragmentation risk (non-unity among parties)
causal-factors.rationale: Opposition fragmentation risk can erode the 2/3 chances if parties fail to unite; reports of groups stepping aside to back TISZA reflect this dynamic ([ft.com](https://www.ft.com/content/85210187-c757-4432-bb57-6b636a669e72?utm_source=openai))

causal-factors.name: Opposition consolidation around the Tisza platform and withdrawals of other parties
causal-factors.rationale: A unified anti-Orban vote behind Tisza reduces vote-splitting and concentrates anti-Fidesz support, as highlighted by late-February 2026 reporting.

causal-factors.name: Polls showing Tisza leading or closing the gap against Fidesz in late Feb 2026
causal-factors.rationale: Divergent but sometimes leading poll readings for Tisza suggest momentum that could translate into more seats if sustained.

causal-factors.name: Electoral system bias that heavily favors the leading party (winner-compensation rules)
causal-factors.rationale: Historical analysis shows the system converts a plurality of votes into outsized seat shares for the largest party, making a 2/3 majority harder to achieve for any coalition.

causal-factors.name: Turnout and voter-concentration dynamics among 'certain voters' for Tisza
causal-factors.rationale: Some polls indicate stronger intensity and potential turnout among certain Tisza supporters, which could bolster seat gains if mobilized.

synthesis: The objections reveal credible pathways to a 2/3 majority via structural disproportionality and potential opposition unity, suggesting the ensemble underestimates tail possibilities. A modest upward recalibration is warranted while polling volatility keeps the scenario uncertain.
